fields.label: Groups ×4
rows: Enclosure gaskets and moulded insulator covers produced to your drawing. The gasket is one input to your enclosure’s ingress test; the dielectric specification comes from the compound datasheet or from testing you commission.
Grommets and pass-through seals sized to your panel thickness and cable diameter, in open, blind, multi-hole and bulkhead configurations.

fields.note:
Four groups, four groups — no count change, one rewritten and two extended.
Card 1 is the substantive edit and it is the most important sentence on this page. The live card claims that Margo’s parts “maintain ingress protection and dielectric separation” — two performance claims, neither backed by any test Margo publishes. The replacement says what the part is and where each specification comes from, which is accurate and more useful to a panel builder: the gasket feeds their IP test, and the dielectric number comes from the compound supplier. It also protects the claim that remains — “moulded insulator covers produced to your drawing” is a real capability and it reads as one

notes: An IP rating belongs to a tested enclosure, not to a gasket. No component supplier can promise an IP class for someone else’s box, and a panel builder knows it — which is why saying so plainly builds more confidence than the claim does.

Dielectric strength is measured to ASTM D149 or IEC 60243, resistivity to ASTM D257. Naming the standards without claiming the data is the same discipline used for biocompatibility on the medical page and potable water on the pumps page.
Assembly headings are <h3>. Four named assembly classes, each a searched phrase — switchgear enclosure gasket, panel cable grommet, cabinet door seal.
Inline links, not card links.

fields.label: Intro
paragraphs: Electrical assemblies fail at their seals. Compound and geometry are selected for ingress performance and long-term compression set rather than initial fit alone — a gasket that seals on the bench and relaxes in year three has failed.
leads: Electrical assemblies fail at their seals.
fields.note: 39 words · live is 34 · the opening sentence is kept exactly — it states the stake in five words and it is true; ingress is the dominant failure mode in outdoor and industrial enclosures. “Dielectric behaviour” comes out of the selection list, because Margo does not test it and cannot select against it. The closing clause is added: it explains what “long-term compression set” actually means to a panel builder, which is the point the section is making

fields.label: Cards ×4
rows: Gasket profiles and compounds chosen to hold their sealing force over years of service, not just at first assembly. Compression set measured to ASTM D395 Method B, which we run in-house — it is the number that predicts whether the enclosure still seals in year five.
Silicone from −60 to +220 °C for elevated-temperature enclosures, retaining flexibility across the range. EPDM −40 to +140 °C where the enclosure is weather-exposed rather than hot.
Sealed geometries for enclosures exposed to particulate, moisture and industrial atmospheres. The gasket is one input to your enclosure’s IEC 60529 test; the rating belongs to the assembly.
Adds the standard and the scoping

Isolation mounts and pads that protect sensitive assemblies from mechanical shock. Isolation only begins above about 1.4 times the system natural frequency, so the mount is sized to the mass it carries.
Adds the isolation criterion from the anti-vibration sheet
fields.note:
Four cards, four cards — no count change, all four given the specific that was missing.
Card 1 is retitled. “Ingress Protection” as a card heading reads as a rating claim; the card body is actually about sealing force retention, which is what it should be called — and naming ASTM D395 Method B backs it with a test Margo genuinely runs.
Card 2: a card headed “thermal stability” that states no temperature. Two figures from the locked homepage table fix it, and the EPDM alternative is added because most electrical enclosures are weather-exposed rather than hot.
Card 3 keeps the IP subject and moves the rating to where it belongs

notes: “Electrical assemblies fail at their seals” is the most citable sentence on this page. It is a claim about the sector rather than about Margo, it is true, and it earns everything the section says afterwards.
ASTM D395 Method B is now named on five sheets — leak test, medical, sponge, HVAC and this one — and Margo runs it in-house. One method, five pages, one credibility argument.
The two temperature figures render from the locked homepage compound table.
Retitling card 1 is not cosmetic. A card headed “Ingress Protection” is what an extraction pass lifts as the claim, and the heading is the part most likely to be quoted without its body.
Card titles are <h3>.
